The Commissioner of Police in Bayelsa State, Ajao Adewale, has called for stronger collaboration among government agencies, traditional rulers, civil society organisations and other stakeholders to tackle gender-based violence and protect women and girls in the state. Adewale made the call on Wednesday during a one-day stakeholders’ workshop on Gender-Based Violence organised by the Bayelsa State Police Command through the Gender Unit of the State Criminal Investigation Department at the Command Officers’ Mess, Yenagoa. The workshop, which had the theme, “Together, We Can Stop Gender-Based Crimes in Bayelsa State,” brought together representatives of the Ministry of Women, Children Affairs and Social Development, the National Agency for the Prohibition of Trafficking in Persons, the International Federation of Women Lawyers, civil society organisations, traditional rulers and non-governmental organisations. The police commissioner described gender-based violence as a serious violation of human rights and a threat to the wellbeing of families and society, insisting that its prevention should not be left to the police alone. He said, ” Gender-based violence constitutes a grave violation of human rights and our collective humanity. The abuse or destruction of a woman’s dignity undermines the foundation of our families and society.” Make PUNCH part of your everyday experience. He added, ” A crime against a woman is a crime against humanity. We must therefore work together to ensure that women and girls are protected from every form of violence, abuse and exploitation.” The CP reaffirmed the command’s commitment to the prevention, investigation and prosecution of gender-based crimes, assuring victims and survivors of professional handling of their cases. He urged members of the public to break the culture of silence surrounding sexual and gender-based violence, reject harmful traditional practices and promote respect, equality and responsible behaviour. “The fight against gender-based violence requires the collective responsibility of all stakeholders. We must reject harmful practices, break the culture of silence and encourage victims to speak out and seek justice,” he said. Adewale further challenged participants to translate the resolutions and recommendations of the workshop into practical measures, stronger partnerships and sustained public enlightenment. He said the ultimate objective was to create a safer environment where women and girls could live, learn and thrive without fear of violence, abuse or exploitation. The workshop featured lectures, presentations and deliberations on strategies for preventing and responding to sexual and gender-based violence in Bayelsa State. The Director of Women Affairs in the state Ministry of Women, Children Affairs and Social Development, Mrs Atotu Yemi Nyinawemi, representatives of NAPTIP and FIDA, among others, attended the event.
